CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Steven W. Huang, DDS, Mayor  www.CityofSanMarino.org
Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone

Tony Chou, Council Member  City Hall Council Chamber

Calvin Lo, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive
Steve Talt, Council Member  San Marino, CA 91108

Philippe Eskandar, City Manager

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 10, 2024 AT 6:00 PM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org or by phone at
(626) 300-0705 prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City
will do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Visit www.CityofSanMarino.org/Zoom

How to offer public comment from home:

  Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org until
  3:00 p.m. the day of the meeting. Written public comment received by 3:00 p.m. will
  be distributed to City Council during the meeting. Any comments received after 3:00

   p.m. will be included in the public comment record but not provided to City Council
  at the meeting.
  Written public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us
  teleconference module during the meeting. Written Zoom comments will be accepted
  after the in-person comments.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Talt, Vice Mayor Shepherd
Romey, and Mayor Huang

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City
Hall, 2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive,
and the Stoneman Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the
City’s website: http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council
by completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the
meeting. At this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on
the agenda. Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on
issues not on the meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor
reserves the right to place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow
up on such items.

CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of
any upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READINGS

This action permits the City Council to act on ordinances and resolutions without having
to read the entire text of the ordinance or resolution. The title of an ordinance on
First Reading must be read in its entirety. An ordinance on Second Reading does not
require having the title read.  However, the City Council may request that an
ordinance or resolution be read in its entirety before taking any action.

AGENDA – JANUARY 10, 2024  PAGE 2 of 5
   NEW BUSINESS

 1.  FIND THE LIFT STATION IMPROVEMENT PROJECT EXEMPT FROM
  REVIEW UNDER THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT
  (CEQA) PURSUANT TO SECTION 15301(B) OF TITLE 14, CHAPTER 3
  OF THE CALIFORNIA CODE OF REGULATIONS (CLASS 1, EXISTING
  FACILITIES  EXEMPTION),  APPROVAL  OF  THE  PLANS  AND
  SPECIFICATIONS AVAILABLE AT THE OFFICE OF THE CITY CLERK AND
  AT THE DAIS, AWARD OF A CONSTRUCTION AGREEMENT TO CWS
  SYSTEMS, INC. FOR THE LIFT STATION IMPROVEMENT PROJECT NO.
  21-8022, IN THE TOTAL AMOUNT (BASE BID PLUS ALTERNATE BIDS
  A1 & A2) OF $2,276,000, AND REJECT ALL OTHER BIDS; AWARD OF A
  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  FOR  CONSTRUCTION
  MANAGEMENT AND INSPECTION SERVICES TO Z&K CONSULTANTS IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $230,000; APPROVAL OF AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO THE
  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICE  AGREEMENT  WITH  DUDEK  FOR
  CONSTRUCTION  SUPPORT  IN  THE  AMOUNT  OF  $45,500;
  AUTHORIZATION FOR PARKS AND PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR/CITY
  ENGINEER TO APPROVE CONTINGENCIES IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO
  EXCEED $250,600; AND APPROPRIATION OF AN ADDITIONAL
  $1,571,181 TO ACCOUNT #394-44-4600-8022 FROM THE CIP FUND
  BALANCE RESERVES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council 1) find the Lift Station
  Improvement Project exempt from review under the California Environmental Quality
  Act (CEQA), 2) approve the Plans and Specifications available at the office of the City
  Clerk and at the dais, 3) award a Construction Agreement to CWS Systems, Inc., 4)
  award a Professional Services Agreement for construction management and
  inspection services to Z&K Consultants, 5) approve Amendment No. 3 to the
  Professional Services Agreement with Dudek for construction support services, and 6)
  authorize the Parks and Public Works Director/City Engineer to approve contract
  change orders and other contingencies in an amount not to exceed $250,600. If the
  Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to 1) find the Lift Station Improvement Project exempt from review under
  the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15301(b) of Title
  14, Chapter 3 of the California Code of Regulations (Class 1, Existing Facilities
  exemption), 2) approve the Plans and Specifications available at the office of the City
  Clerk and at the dais, 3) award a Construction Agreement to CWS Systems, Inc., for
  the Lift Station Improvement Project No. 21-8022 in the amount of $2,276,000, and
  reject all other bids, 4) award a Professional Services Agreement for construction
  management and inspection services to Z&K Consultants in the amount of $230,000,
  5) approve Amendment No. 3 to the Professional Services Agreement with Dudek in
  the amount of $45,500, and 6) authorize the Parks and Public Works Director/City
  Engineer to approve contract change orders and other contingencies in an amount
  not to exceed $250,600, and 7) appropriate an additional $1,571,181 to account
  #394-44-4600-8022 (Lift Station Improvements) from the CIP fund balance
  reserves.

AGENDA – JANUARY 10, 2024  PAGE 3 of 5
   CONSENT CALENDAR

 2.  APPROVAL OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ROGERS,
  ANDERSON, MALODY & SCOTT, LLP AND APPOINTING TERRY SHEA
  INTERIM FINANCE DIRECTOR

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Professional
  Services Agreement with Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP and concur with the
  appointment of Terry Shea as Interim Finance Director. If Council concurs, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the Professional Services Agreement with Rogers, Anderson,
  Malody & Scott, LLP and concur with the appointment of Terry Shea as Interim
  Finance Director.”

 3.  APPROVAL OF PURCHASE OF ONE POLICE VEHICLE FROM NATIONAL
  AUTO FLEET IN THE AMOUNT OF $64,810.58

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve the purchase of a
  Police Department vehicles from National Auto Fleet in the amount of $64,810.58.

  “I move to approve the purchase of a Chevrolet Tahoe for the Police Department
  from National Auto Fleet in the amount of $64,810.58.”

 4.  APPROVE AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO EXTEND AGREEMENT FOR LANCE,
  SOLL & LUNGHARD, LLP, TO PERFORM PROFESSIONAL AUDITING
  SERVICES FOR THE FISCAL YEARS ENDING JUNE 30, 2024 AND 2025

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve Amendment No. 1 to the
  Agreement with Lance Soll & Lunghard to extend the term through December 31,
  2025, for the FYE June 30, 2024, and FYE June 30, 2025, Audit Services and
  authorize the City Manager to approve and execute the amendment and any other
  documents necessary to effectuate the contract. If the City Council concurs with
  staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve Amendment No. 1 to the Agreement with Lance Soll & Lunghard
  to extend the term through December 31, 2025, for the FYE June 30, 2024, and FYE
  June 30, 2025, Audit Services and authorize and direct the City Manager to execute
  Amendment No. 1 to the professional services agreement with Lance, Soll &
  Lunghard, LLP for the City’s Financial Statement Auditing Services for two additional
  one-year extensions.”

 5.  CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF NOVEMBER
  2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

AGENDA – JANUARY 10, 2024  PAGE 4 of 5
   “I move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of
  November 2023.”

 6.  RECEIVE AND FILE  MONTHLY  DISBURSEMENTS  REPORT  FOR
  DECEMBER 2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of December 2023. If the City Council concurs
  with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of
  December 2023.”

 7.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the December 2023
  minutes. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to approve the minutes of the special meeting of December 13, 2023, and
  the regular meeting of December 13, 2023.”

 8.  RATIFICATION OF THE FY 2022-23 CALIFORNIA STATE LIBRARY
  REPORT

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council ratify the FY 2022-23 California
  State Library Report. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to ratify the FY 2022-23 California State Library Report.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

ADJOURNMENT
